bear.text: EBITDA margin declined by 170 basis points to 11.2% in Q1 FY27, a contraction attributed to a sharp rise in copper prices during the quarter.
Receivable days increased from 78 to 96 over the last year, primarily due to slower payments from two large state utility customers.
The company received a GST demand order for ₹46.3 crore, including interest and penalty, related to input tax credits claimed for FY2020-21 and FY2021-22.
Management notes that price-variation clauses in about two-thirds of contracts reset with a lag of one to two quarters, which may delay full cost pass-through.

bull.text: Revenue from operations grew 18.0% year-on-year to ₹1,248 crore in Q1 FY27.
The order book stood at ₹3,900 crore as of 30 June 2026, up from ₹3,150 crore a year ago.
Management states the new Bharuch plant, which adds about 30% to cable capacity, is on track to begin commercial production in Q3 FY27.
Exports contributed 21% of revenue in Q1 FY27, an increase from 16% in the same period last year.

open_questions.text: The company's press release reports Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹1,248 crore, while a news article reports ₹1,428 crore. What explains this discrepancy in the reported revenue figures?
Management intends to appeal the ₹46.3 crore GST demand and states it does not expect a material impact. What is the timeline and potential outcome of this appeal?
Management believes data-centre cables, currently 9% of domestic revenue, can double in two years. What specific market conditions or contracts support this growth expectation?

snapshot.text: Sarvottam Cables Ltd is a manufacturer of power cables, wires and conductors listed on the NSE.
For Q1 FY27, the company reported revenue of ₹1,248 crore and profit after tax of ₹82 crore.
As of June 2026, promoters held 58.2% of the company, with 4.1% of that holding pledged, down from 11.5% in June 2025.
Institutional ownership increased in June 2026, with FIIs holding 11.8% and DIIs holding 14.6% of the shares.
